value: 90% of recorded positions on the dark side of the chamber under UVA light (395-400 nm), i.e. avoidance of UV; 10% on the dark side under white light
units: % of recorded positions on dark side
method: light-side/dark-side choice in an elongate blacked-out flow-through chamber (30 x 7.5 x 7.5 cm, Edwards Aquifer water about 1.5 mL/s); one end unblacked to admit light from external 9 W LED bulbs on a 12:12 h timer; beetle placed in the middle and its position recorded once a day between 09:00 and 11:00 on two or three consecutive days; binomial mixed-effects logistic regression with container and day as random effects, white light as baseline
conditions: wild-collected adults from the Comal Springs system (2023-2024); 9 or 10 beetles per treatment (UV n = 10; Table 1 lists 18 dark and 2 light records for UV, 2 dark and 18 light for white); the light treatment was on the same side in all chambers, so side was not randomised; individuals were checked on consecutive days within an experiment and some were reused across experiments without tracking; UV versus white baseline P = 0.0017, but red (16.7% dark, P = 0.71) did not differ from white, and blue (48.1%), green (57.7%) and a no-light control (47.4%) were near half and differed from white (P = 0.038, 0.022, 0.043); the Discussion says the white response may be a response to its red component and the paper does not give the number of observations as a single stated figure

value: no recognition of the odour of three snakes (Natrix maura, Rhinechis scalaris, Macroprotodon mauritanicus) by tongue-flick and 15 other scored behaviours in three islet populations; no significant differences for any variable
method: each lizard in a 60 x 40 x 40 cm terrarium on absorbent paper holding the scent treatment (snake odour or odourless control), six marked sectors, 15 min trial under a 75 W bulb at 30 C, one trial per day between 08:00 and 17:00, each lizard given each of four treatments once in a random order; Friedman tests across treatments
conditions: wild-caught in Menorca in summer 2013; 24 lizards per population (12 males, 12 females) from Colom, Aire and Binicodrell islets, sexes pooled after Mann-Whitney U tests showed no difference (P > 0.05); tongue-flick means per treatment were close (for example Colom control 72.75, Natrix 74.08, Rhinechis 74.79, Macroprotodon 69.33; Friedman P = 0.765, 0.244 and 0.110 for the three populations, from Tables 1 to 3); the Discussion reports that the introduced Podarcis siculus did respond to Macroprotodon scent (not tongue-flick, which did not differ there), so the odour treatments elicited a response in another species; the paper does not separately validate the odours in P. lilfordi

value: an intact olfactory system is required for sensing copper: copper avoidance was lost in tissue-glue anosmic fish
method: I-maze 55 x 11.5 x 14 cm with three zones and 3 L river water; one fish per trial, 5 min acclimation, copper (nominal about 10 ug/L, 62.7 nM copper sulphate, calculated not measured) and blank solutions diffused for 3 min, position recorded every 10 s for 5 min; the copper end chosen by coin flip; anosmia by 1-2 uL tissue glue in each nostril under MS-222 anaesthesia, at least 24 h recovery; proportion-of-time index, t tests
conditions: adults from a breeding colony (age, size and sex not reported); 14 fish per group (control, mock-anosmic with water in the nostrils, anosmic) plus a preliminary group of 9 intact fish that avoided copper (t(8) = -2.55, p = 0.034); control avoided the copper arm (t(13) = -3.66, p = 0.006), mock-anosmic avoided it (t = -5.71, p < 0.001), anosmic fish did not (t(13) = 1.23, p = 0.24); no verification of olfactory loss beyond the procedure and no measurement of the copper concentration; the Discussion says copper may damage the olfactory epithelium rather than act as an odorant and that the earlier whitefish avoidance may reflect the concentration gradient, so the mechanism is left unresolved; the quoted Abstract sentence is worded for fish in general, the species-specific results are in the Abstract and Results; this is behavioural avoidance of a dissolved metal, not a response to a natural odour
